@@ -0,0 +1,52 @@
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import typing as t
+
+from ._compat import _find_binary_reader
+
+
+def input_byte_count(
+    input: str | bytes | t.IO[t.Any] | None, charset: str = "utf-8"
+) -> int:
+    """Return the number of bytes ``input`` would provide as input to
+    :meth:`click.testing.CliRunner.invoke`.
+
+    Accepts the same input shapes as :func:`click.testing.make_input_stream`,
+    but measures the encoded size instead of returning a stream.
+
+    -   ``None`` is zero bytes.
+    -   ``str`` is encoded with ``charset``.
+    -   ``bytes`` and ``bytearray`` are measured directly.
+    -   A readable object is read to the end and its data measured. Binary
+        streams, or text streams with a binary ``buffer``, are read as bytes.
+        Other streams must return ``str``, which is encoded with ``charset``.
+
+    :param input: The input to measure.
+    :param charset: The encoding used for text input.
+    :raises TypeError: If ``input`` is not a supported type, or a stream
+        does not return ``str`` or ``bytes``.
+    """
+    if input is None:
+        return 0
+
+    if isinstance(input, str):
+        return len(input.encode(charset))
+
+    if isinstance(input, (bytes, bytearray)):
+        return len(input)
+
+    if hasattr(input, "read"):
+        reader = _find_binary_reader(input)
+        data = (reader if reader is not None else input).read()
+
+        if isinstance(data, str):
+            return len(data.encode(charset))
+
+        if isinstance(data, (bytes, bytearray)):
+            return len(data)
+
+        raise TypeError(
+            f"Input stream returned {type(data).__name__!r}, expected 'str' or 'bytes'."
+        )
+
+    raise TypeError(f"Unsupported input type {type(input).__name__!r}.")
diff --git a/tests/test_input_byte_count.py b/tests/test_input_byte_count.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..e585ff8
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/test_input_byte_count.py
@@ -0,0 +1,76 @@
+import io
+
+import pytest
+
+from click.input_byte_count import input_byte_count
+
+
+def test_none():
+    assert input_byte_count(None) == 0
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("value", "charset", "expect"),
+    [
+        ("", "utf-8", 0),
+        ("abc", "utf-8", 3),
+        ("\u00e9", "utf-8", 2),
+        ("\u00e9", "latin-1", 1),
+        ("\u20ac", "utf-16-le", 2),
+    ],
+)
+def test_str(value, charset, expect):
+    assert input_byte_count(value, charset) == expect
+
+
+def test_str_default_charset():
+    assert input_byte_count("\u2603") == 3
+
+
+def test_str_unencodable():
+    with pytest.raises(UnicodeEncodeError):
+        input_byte_count("\u2603", "ascii")
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("value", [b"", b"\xff\x00abc", bytearray(b"abcd")])
+def test_bytes(value):
+    assert input_byte_count(value, "ascii") == len(value)
+
+
+def test_binary_stream_consumed():
+    stream = io.BytesIO(b"hello\n")
+    assert input_byte_count(stream) == 6
+    assert stream.read() == b""
+
+
+def test_binary_stream_partially_read():
+    stream = io.BytesIO(b"hello")
+    stream.read(2)
+    assert input_byte_count(stream) == 3
+
+
+def test_text_stream_with_buffer():
+    stream = io.TextIOWrapper(io.BytesIO("\u00e9\n".encode("latin-1")), "latin-1")
+    assert input_byte_count(stream, "utf-8") == 2
+
+
+def test_text_stream_without_buffer():
+    stream = io.StringIO("\u00e9t\u00e9")
+    assert input_byte_count(stream) == 5
+    assert input_byte_count(io.StringIO("\u00e9t\u00e9"), "latin-1") == 3
+    assert stream.read() == ""
+
+
+def test_stream_bad_read():
+    class Reader:
+        def read(self, size=-1):
+            return 42
+
+    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="int"):
+        input_byte_count(Reader())
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("value", [1, 1.5, ["a"], object()])
+def test_unsupported(value):
+    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="Unsupported"):
+        input_byte_count(value)
notes:
input_byte_count mirrors make_input_stream's input shapes (None, str, bytes, readable) but returns len of the encoded data; readable inputs are read via click's _find_binary_reader when a binary layer exists, otherwise read as text and encoded with charset, and anything else raises TypeError. No BytesIO is constructed and no handle is returned; tests in tests/test_input_byte_count.py.
